summary: Soi Nana in Bangkok's Chinatown is a short, atmospheric lane of converted shophouses with cocktail bars, Thai and Chinese inspired drinks, food and occasional live music. Plan a bar crawl rather than a single ticketed attraction, and make sure your map pin is Chinatown's Soi Nana, not Nana Plaza or Sukhumvit Soi 4.
whyGo: The lane puts several distinct independent bars within an easy stroll, from gin and local-herb cocktails to Chinese-Thai comfort food and live Thai music.
Its old shophouse setting gives an evening out more neighborhood character than a standalone cocktail venue.
bestFor: A small-group evening of drinks and casual bar-hopping, especially for visitors interested in Bangkok's cocktail scene.
Pairing dinner or street food in Yaowarat with one or two nearby bars.
skipIf: You want a quiet, family-focused evening, step-free venues, or a guaranteed seat for a large group.
You are seeking a daytime attraction or a scheduled cultural performance; music and crowd levels vary by venue and night.
duration: Allow 2–3 hours for a meal and two or three stops; the lane itself is small and can be walked through quickly.
cost: No street admission fee. Budget roughly ฿300–600 per person for one or two drinks, with food extra; this is a planning estimate, not a quoted current menu price. Time Out lists Ba Hao in price band 2/4 and some example snacks, but prices and menus can change.
hours: Individual venues set their own schedules. Ba Hao's official site lists daily opening at 17:00, until midnight Sunday–Thursday and 01:00 Friday–Saturday. Time Out's March 2026 guide lists Tep Bar daily 18:00–midnight and several other venues with later hours. Check the specific bar's current social page before travelling.
bestTime: Arrive around 18:00–19:00 for dinner and a better chance of a seat; Tep Bar is reportedly livelier with performances later in the evening. Fridays and Saturdays are likely to be busier, so start early.
gettingThere: Take the MRT Blue Line to Wat Mangkon, in the heart of Chinatown, then walk toward Soi Nana around Maitrichit Road; allow about 10–15 minutes from the station as a route-planning estimate. MRT Wat Mangkon Exit 1 serves Plaeng Nam Road, and the station's other exits serve Charoen Krung and nearby streets. Traffic in Chinatown can be slow, so MRT is usually simpler than a taxi at peak evening time. Confirm your map destination says Soi Nana, Chinatown.
booking: There is no admission or booking for walking the lane. For a table, especially on a Friday or Saturday, contact the chosen venue directly; Ba Hao lists reservations at +66 62 464 5468. Teens of Thailand is described by Time Out as having only 15 seats, so expect a wait or choose another bar if full. No December 2026 special event schedule was available in the sources checked.
accessibility: The public lane is narrow and the bars occupy older shophouses; some have tight interiors or stairs. Step-free access, accessible toilets and seating arrangements are not established by the sources checked. This may be difficult for wheelchair users or visitors who cannot manage steps; contact an individual bar before visiting.
practicalTips: Start with a destination pin for Ba Hao, 8 Soi Nana, Maitrichit Road, or another chosen venue; the lane has the same name as the nightlife district on Sukhumvit.
Dress casually and comfortably for Bangkok's evening heat. No formal dress code was found; avoid assuming every small bar can accommodate large bags or groups.
Check current opening hours and menus on the day. Ba Hao's official listing and Time Out's guide differ slightly on closing times, so use the venue's direct channel for a late-night plan.
Keep the group small and walk carefully through the compact lane; leave room for residents, staff and other guests.
decemberNotes: December 2026 venue hours and events cannot be guaranteed this far ahead. Bangkok is generally more comfortable for evening walking than in the hottest season, but the lane's bars can be busy around weekends and holiday dates. Recheck hours and make any table request directly with a venue shortly before the visit.
uncertainties: Opening hours in online guides are not fully consistent and may change before December 2026; the venue should confirm its schedule directly.
Drink prices above are only a planning estimate; no current complete menu pricing was verified.
No reliable venue-by-venue step-free access or accessible toilet information was found.
